exposure: Timing of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) diagnosis (before 20 weeks of gestation vs. at or after 24 weeks of gestation)
cohort: The study analyzed 1,275 mother-infant pairs from a GDM registry in Japan, with 924 women undergoing postpartum glucose intolerance testing.
finding: Women diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus before 20 weeks of gestation (EGDM) had a significantly higher risk of postpartum glucose intolerance than those diagnosed at or after 24 weeks (LGDM), and overweight/obese EGDM women also experienced a higher rate of preterm birth.
birth_weight: Outcomes included small for gestational age (SGA) and large for gestational age (LGA), which are typically defined by birth weight percentiles.
gest_age: The exposure was defined by gestational age at GDM diagnosis (before 20 weeks vs. at or after 24 weeks), and outcomes included preterm birth and small for gestational age.
